title: How the March on Washington Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom (August 28, 1963). They cover A. Philip Randolph and the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, the 1941 Executive Order 8802 and Fair Employment Practices Committee, the coalition of the Big Six civil rights groups, Anna Arnold Hedgeman's role in bringing King and Randolph together, Bayard Rustin's logistics and planning, fears of violence and media coverage, the Birmingham campaign and Medgar Evers's murder, criticism from Stokely Carmichael and Malcolm X, the celebrity performers and program, John Lewis's watered-down speech, King's "I Have a Dream" speech and its copyright, and the march's influence on the Civil Rights Act, Voting Rights Act and Great Society. The episode closes with a listener mail about Jim Henson and a clip of King's speech.
topics: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
Martin Luther King Jr. I Have a Dream speech

entities.name: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom

segments.title: Opening banter and context
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the episode's topic, its timing near the MLK holiday, and their personal reflections on civil rights history.

segments.title: A. Philip Randolph and the Pullman porters
segments.summary: Background on A. Philip Randolph, the Pullman porters' working conditions, the founding of the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, and its 1937 labor agreement with the Pullman Company.

segments.title: 1941 march threat and Executive Order 8802
segments.summary: Randolph's earlier march proposal led FDR to issue Executive Order 8802 creating the Fair Employment Practices Committee, which opened defense jobs to Black workers; the committee was later dissolved.
topics: FDR New Deal and civil rights

segments.title: Organizing coalition and permit request
segments.summary: The march was organized by a coalition of groups, Randolph wrote to Interior Secretary Stewart Udall requesting a permit, and the route was set to end at the Lincoln Memorial. The Big Six groups are listed, and Anna Arnold Hedgeman is credited with bringing King and Randolph together.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode message break before the discussion of media fears about the march.

segments.title: Media fears, the Birmingham campaign and Medgar Evers
segments.summary: Mainstream media feared violence and riots, but the march was peaceful. The hosts describe the Birmingham campaign, police violence against children, and the killing of Medgar Evers two months earlier.

segments.title: Bayard Rustin and planning the march
segments.summary: Bayard Rustin is described as the key organizer who planned the march in about two months, wrote a manual for bus captains, ran the program, and influenced King toward nonviolence. The hosts also discuss white and Jewish participation and the Kennedy administration's request to cancel.

segments.title: Criticism from militant leaders and John Lewis's speech
segments.summary: Stokely Carmichael and Malcolm X criticized the march as not radical enough. John Lewis's speech was toned down by other leaders, including the Catholic Archbishop of Washington. The hosts discuss the tension between moderate and militant approaches.

segments.title: Celebrity performers and program
segments.summary: The hosts list celebrities and performers at the march, including Marlon Brando, Charlton Heston, Bob Dylan, Joan Baez, Peter, Paul and Mary, Mahalia Jackson, and others, and the MCs Ossie Davis and Ruby Dee.

segments.title: I Have a Dream speech and aftermath
segments.summary: King's speech, its bad check metaphor and improvised dream section, its later fame after King's assassination, and the copyright issues over the speech. The hosts also discuss LBJ passing the Civil Rights Act, Voting Rights Act and Great Society.

segments.title: Listener mail about Jim Henson
segments.summary: Listener Chris writes about the Jim Henson episode, his dog Jupiter's death, and his documentary project Footnotes; the hosts close the mail section with contact information.

segments.title: Closing snippet
segments.summary: The episode closes with a short audio clip of King's speech.
